label: M-04
title: exchangeRate re-prices only the stable leg: a hard 1x issuance floor no setting can go below, an unbounded ceiling, and a silent re-scaling of what maxMintPerDay permits
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss. Two operational impacts: (a) the natural remediation lever for over-issuance does not work - at exchangeRate = 0.10e18 the protocol still emits 1.10 phUSD per $1 taken in, and the uncollateralised component is entirely unaffected, so there is NO rate that makes annihilation backing-neutral and the only true stop is setStablecoinEnabled(false), a full stop with no intermediate setting; (b) changing the rate silently re-scales what maxMintPerDay permits (at rate 0.5e18 the effective multiplier moves from 2x to 3x the entered number), so the M-03 mis-sizing drifts underneath the operator.
attackPath: 1. Operator observes phUSD dilution and reaches for exchangeRate as a throttle - the obvious lever.

2. The stablecoin PULLED is rate-independent (decimals only, :254-256) and the antimatter leg is always exactly `amount` (:236); only the stable leg's phUSD is rate-scaled. Total issuance per unit of stablecoin received is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18), which is bounded BELOW by 1x.
3. Dilution continues at >= 1x forever while the operator believes the throttle is engaged.
4. Simultaneously the daily cap's effective multiplier has changed without any change to maxMintPerDay, and neither side documents the coupling.
classification.likelihood: Medium - it bites exactly when an operator responds to an issuance problem, i.e. at the worst moment.
classification.assumptions: Operator treats exchangeRate as an issuance throttle, which is what its name and position suggest.
classification.externalRequirements: An owner rate change. Non-malicious and non-obvious in its consequences.

justification: MEDIUM as an operational hazard, with the boundary stated explicitly so this is not read as an owner-malice finding. The 'unbounded ceiling' half alone (rate = 1.5e18 emits 2.5 phUSD per $1 from one un-timelocked owner call) would be LOW on its own - an owner raising a rate and getting more issuance is an OBVIOUS consequence, and Law 3 suppresses obvious owner misuse. The Medium rests entirely on the two SURPRISING halves: that lowering the rate can never reach parity (a safety lever that silently cannot do the job it appears to do), and that a rate change silently re-prices a different control. Neither is documented on either side. Surprise => footgun => in scope at honest severity, and 'the protocol's issuance control does not function as a control' is a C4 Medium function impact. Not High: no theft, no direct asset risk, requires an owner action, and the harm is realised only through the dilution channel already priced in M-02. The Halmos PROOF that the no-residue property holds for EVERY uint256 exchangeRate is retained as scoping evidence, not as reassurance: it establishes that an arbitrary rate does not strand assets, which isolates the hazard as economic/operational rather than a settlement defect.
recommendation: Add a sanity bound in Antimatter itself - it already reads exchangeRate's sibling fields at :250 and can assert mintedForStable is within tolerance of `amount`, so a fat-fingered or oversized rate fails closed.
Alternatively scale the antimatter leg by the same rate at :236 so the single knob governs the whole output.

evidence.symbolic: halmos PROVED (tier3/halmos-p2-noresidue-unbounded.txt) the no-residue property holds for EVERY uint256 exchangeRate - i.e. an arbitrary rate does not strand assets. The hazard is economic, not a settlement defect, which this proof isolates.
evidence.profitabilityBoundary: the annihilator's loop (DEDUP-004) stays profitable whenever p > 1/(1 + rate/1e18): p > $1.00 at rate 0, p > $0.50 at rate 1e18.

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

additionalContext.rootCause: The stablecoin PULLED is rate-independent (decimals only) and the antimatter leg is always exactly `amount`; only the stable leg's phUSD is rate-scaled. Total issuance per unit of stablecoin received is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18). Antimatter applies no sanity bound of its own even though it already reads the config struct at :250.
additionalContext.impact: (a) THROTTLE FLOOR: the natural response to over-issuance is to lower the rate, but at rate=0.10e18 the protocol still emits 1.10 phUSD per $1 taken in, and the unbacked component is completely unaffected. There is no rate that makes annihilation backing-neutral; the only lever that stops dilution is setStablecoinEnabled(false) - a full stop with no intermediate setting. (b) AMPLIFIER: at rate=1.5e18 the pair emits 2.5 phUSD per $1, from a single unbounded, un-timelocked owner call.
additionalContext.interactionWithDedup002: Changing the rate silently re-scales the effective daily cap: at rate 0.5e18 the effective maxMintPerDay multiplier moves from 2x to 3x the entered number. Two knobs interacting in a direction neither is documented to move.
additionalContext.footgunTest: Law 3 - surprise on both counts: that lowering the rate cannot bring issuance to parity, and that changing the rate silently re-scales what maxMintPerDay permits. Neither is documented on either side. In scope.
additionalContext.safeConfigGuidance: Treat exchangeRate as an amplitude control on the BACKED leg only, never as an issuance throttle. Keep it at or below 1e18 on every annihilatable stablecoin. Recompute maxMintPerDay as intendedIssuance / (1 + exchangeRate/1e18) on every rate change. To actually stop dilution use setStablecoinEnabled(false).

mergeAction: 3-way consolidation. AM-LOCAL-005 is the profiler's local half ('unbounded owner parameter'), MR-05 is the code-scanner's parked deferral of the same lever, ECON-003 supplies the operator-lever model. All three cite the rate-independence of :254-256 and :236. ECON-003 itself states 'that entry records the local half; this one adds the operator-lever model'.
